institutionName: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Studying abroad in USA was an opportunity that I couldn't say no to. I was hoping for an adventure, and to study at a high-profile university at the same time.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All in all it is really something I would recommend to everyone.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy to find information. It's hard to remember everything though - write things down in your notes app.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
My roommate (who was on his third year) helped me a lot, I don't know what I would have done in the beginning without him. He showed me around, and took me to a lot of places, games, etc. 

Check your emails! Both from your home institution and from your institution abroad.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: A small percentage of all the information was either hard to understand or only explained briefly. But everything is going to work out fine!

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Very easy for me - I might have been lucky. I ended up living with the first one I approached. This is what I did:
1. Go on Facebook
2. Find "UNC Chapel Hill Subleases, Roommates, Off Campus Housing & Apartments"
3. Find something on there that's affordable, close to campus, and with one or more nice-looking potential roommates. 
4. Arrange a Skype/Zoom meeting and work it out together.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: My roommate was three years younger than me - I was 23. It showed quite often.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Again, I was very lucky.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy to find, but very stressful. You have to be quick if you want the courses you want. Plan alternatives accordingly.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Everyone gets the chance to enroll in the courses that they want. That's a lot of students registering for the same courses at the same time. If you succeeded, good for you. But if the classes are already full you need to be quick with the alternatives. You get two chances(waves) to enroll, so don't stress too much if weren't too successful the first time.

The teachers respond really quickly, so send them an email if you have any questions. Find their @ on the university website.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Instructional emails and attached PDF's. Be sure to read and understand the attached files.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It worked out in the end. I emailed two professors and they were both really nice and let me on their courses. Just be polite, tell them who you are, why you want to enroll in their course. 99% of the time they'll let you on their course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enroll on an LFIT (Lifetime Fitness) course. It's just 1 credit, but you get to play sports, run, or whatever you choose to do. Check the university course catalogue.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were many great courses available.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had one course on 100-level and three courses on 200-level. That might have been too easy academically. A friend of mine from back home had some courses on 300-level and that was challenging, she told me.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The class sessions don't differ too much. More homework compared to back home though. In some courses a part of your grade is based on proof that you read/made your homework.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
181 Sports Psychology
206 Analysis of Sport Skills II
273 Research in Exercise and Sport Science
276 Human Physiology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
276 Human Physiology was by far the best course I had all semester. I learned a lot. Tough course, but Dr. Ondrak was a really good teacher. I really liked her style of teaching. 

273 Research in Exercise and Sport Science was disappointing though. The professor was 77 y/o and taught via zoom. Difficult to stay focused for 1,5 hours when someone is talking about statistics on Zoom.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There were more fees that I had to pay than I thought there would be. As an example I just paid 9 usd to get my transcript (a PDF file) from the host institution.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Restaurants and take-out is cheaper compared to Copenhagen.

Get yourself a VIC-card and save 5-10 dollars when you grocery shop. The card is free, just tell them you're a student.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UNC has a tradition of sports - so if you like sports you'll be automatically welcome.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Intramural sports are nice.

Besides that I played a round of disc golf five days a week. Their course is really nice - both if you're new or not to the sport. I've gotten to know a handful of very nice people on the course.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend meeting people through sports. I did it through disc golf and soccer, but you can basically sign up for anything and you're gonna meet some nice people there.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Charlotte is a very nice "small" city. Raleigh is boring I would say. 

Me and the boys went road tripping through Savannah, Georgia down to Saint Augustine, Florida. That was a really good trip. Rent a car or go with someone with a car - most Americans have their own car.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Once they detect an accent and that you're from abroad they curious.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Smile, choose a chair next to some nice-looking people, and hope for the best. If you're lucky you end up sitting next to a friend, and if you're not - change your seat next class!

Intramural sports is also something I would definitely recommend.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Quick tip: Don't discuss politics or anything similar to that with Americans. I tried to avoid it all through the semester and I am pretty sure I managed to avoid some sticky situations. 

Be nice and they will be nice to you. That goes everywhere I guess.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They're extremely friendly and welcoming. "Do you want to come with me to the game tomorrow? I can pick you up if you need a ride..." They're also more talkative and curious than most Danes. They WILL ask questions :))

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. I upgraded my phone/data deal in order to be able to data roam in the US. Although they stated they would cancel it after a few weeks (the deal was only for roaming on vacations), they never did. I ended up not paying very much the entire semester. That also meant I didn't need to acquire an American phone number or eSIM. 

2. Americans are mostly really nice, but I found it a lot easier to socialize with fellow Europeans. Trust me, you're not the only European, Scandinavian, or Dane. I was lucky to become very good friends with two Germans, one Swede, one Dutch, and one Dane with whom I met at an introduction meeting for students from abroad. For me at least, it was easier to relax when I was chilling with my European friends compared to Americans. I don't know why.

3. Have fun, find people whose company you enjoy, and don't waste your time. The time goes by fast.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Michael Jordan (Google him if you don't know him lol) went to UNC - they're gonna ask you if you know who he is.

If you want to go to the States, I would definitely recommend UNC.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I got and the memories we now share.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To get enough sleep lol.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I might have been lucky, but I truly feel like that if you follow your guts, you're gonna end up having a good time.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
